issue: Can a felon bring an as-applied Second Amendment challenge to the federal ban on firearm possession by felons, or is § 922(g)(1) categorically constitutional as applied to all felons?

sides.position: Section 922(g)(1) is categorically constitutional as applied to all felons; status-based disqualification of felons is consistent with the historical tradition of firearm regulation.
cases: United States v. Jackson, 110 F.4th 1120 (8th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Hunt, 123 F.4th 697 (4th Cir. 2024)

sides.position: Section 922(g)(1) might be unconstitutional as applied to some felons, so an as-applied challenge is available, depending on whether the defendant's predicate felony is relevantly similar to a historical disqualifying crime.
cases: United States v. Diaz, 116 F.4th 458 (5th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Mitchell, No. 24-60607 (5th Cir. 2025)

this_court: Recognizes that § 922(g)(1) may be unconstitutional as applied to some felons, but is bound by Diaz and rejects the as-applied challenge in this case under that precedent.
quote: An entrenched circuit split has now emerged about its proper application.
cite: United States v. Mitchell, No. 24-60607 (5th Cir. 2025)
